metadata.description: Fourteen plugins, one per classic software engineering book. Each ships 50+ skills, subagents and modes built on the MIT-licensed rule sets from ciembor/agent-rules-books.

plugins.name: clean-code
plugins.description: Robert C. Martin's Clean Code: skills, subagents and modes for naming, small functions, comments, error handling, tests, concurrency and scoped cleanup of touched code.

plugins.name: philosophy-of-design
plugins.description: John Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design: skills, subagents and modes for deep modules, information hiding, narrow interfaces, defining errors away and strategic design.

plugins.name: clean-architecture
plugins.description: Robert C. Martin's Clean Architecture: skills, subagents and modes for dependency direction, use cases, ports and adapters, component design and boundaries that keep business rules independent of frameworks and databases.

plugins.name: code-complete
plugins.description: Steve McConnell's Code Complete: skills, subagents and modes for routine design, data meaning, control flow, defensive programming, testing, debugging and measured tuning.

plugins.name: data-intensive-apps
plugins.description: Designing Data-Intensive Applications by Martin Kleppmann: skills, subagents and modes for data ownership, consistency, retries and replay, schema evolution, replication, partitioning and streams.

plugins.name: ddd
plugins.description: Eric Evans' Domain-Driven Design: skills, subagents and modes for ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, context maps, aggregates, supple design and core-domain focus.

plugins.name: ddd-distilled
plugins.description: Vaughn Vernon's Domain-Driven Design Distilled: skills, subagents and modes for subdomains, bounded contexts, context maps, small aggregates, event storming and DDD without ceremony.

plugins.name: ddd-implementing
plugins.description: Vaughn Vernon's Implementing Domain-Driven Design: skills, subagents and modes for bounded contexts in code, small aggregates, repositories, domain events, application services and anticorruption layers.

plugins.name: enterprise-patterns
plugins.description: Martin Fowler's enterprise application patterns: choose business logic, persistence, transaction, locking, presentation and remoting patterns by force, keep responsibilities separate, and review for the book's forbidden patterns. Unofficial.

plugins.name: refactoring
plugins.description: Refactoring by Martin Fowler: skills, subagents and modes for behavior-preserving change in small, tested steps, with structure kept separate from feature work and cleanup that stops when the change is easy.

plugins.name: refactoring-guru
plugins.description: Refactoring.Guru's smell and technique catalog: diagnose a named smell, apply the smallest safe treatment, verify, and stop before redesign. Skills, subagents and modes built on a paraphrased rule set for coding agents.

plugins.name: release-it
plugins.description: Michael T. Nygard's Release It!: skills, subagents and modes for timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, bulkheads, overload control, safe deployment and observability in services, APIs and queues.

plugins.name: pragmatic-programmer
plugins.description: Hunt and Thomas's The Pragmatic Programmer: skills, subagents and modes for DRY knowledge, orthogonality, tracer bullets, contracts, debugging, automation and owning the result.

plugins.name: legacy-code
plugins.description: Michael Feathers's Working Effectively with Legacy Code: skills, subagents and modes for characterization tests, seams, dependency breaking, sprout and wrap, and changing untested code in small, verified steps.
